speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have experienced any fever, joint pain, or recent sun exposure before these blisters and ulcers appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the blisters or ulcers appear shortly after you started taking captopril? Have you noticed any rash or blistering on your trunk, back, or other parts of your body?

text: I need to clarify the timeline regarding captopril; did the skin lesions appear within days of starting it? Also, can you describe the appearance of the blisters—are they tense or fragile, and do they leave scarring as they heal?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, osteoarthritis. Social history: Has started hiking in the woods on weekends. No relevant travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the blisters on your forearm rupture easily and leave scars, or do they heal without scarring? Also, have you noticed any blistering or erosions inside your mouth, eyes, or on your genitals?

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned pain with eating and intercourse, which strongly suggests mucosal involvement. To confirm this, please tell me if you have visible sores or blistering inside your mouth or on your genitals.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have visible, painful sores or blistering inside your mouth or on your genitals? REQUEST TEST: Tzanck_smear

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Tzanck smear is normal, we can likely rule out herpes simplex or varicella-zoster virus. Given the mucosal involvement and new medication, I suspect an autoimmune blistering disease like pemphigus vulgaris; therefore, I need a definitive tissue diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy_with_Direct_Immunofluorescence

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy_with_Direct_Immunofluorescence: Histopathology shows acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct immunofluorescence reveals intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis. Blood tests confirm the presence of desmoglein antibodies.
